items.headline: 363-unit apartment plan would replace Stevens Creek Blvd offices
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 10 agenda listed The Hanover Company's 363-unit apartment proposal at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, which would replace existing office buildings. The site is on the city's Priority Housing Sites list (Sites 5 and 6) in its 6th Cycle Housing Element, and the project relies on SB 330 and State Density Bonus law.

items.headline: Preschool for up to 192 kids proposed at 855 E. Homestead
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a Special Development Permit to demolish a vacant commercial building on a 1.11-acre site and build a 16,000-square-foot, two-story Primrose Schools childcare and preschool for up to 192 children. The plan includes a new eight-foot masonry wall along the western and part of the southern property lines.

items.headline: Historic Washington Street home eyed for 1,200 sq ft ADU
items.summary: The Historical and Landmarks Commission's November 5 agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street, a Historic Resource Inventory property. The project (PLN26-00020) needs a Significant Property Alteration / Architectural Review and is listed as categorically exempt from CEQA.

items.headline: Historic preservation ordinance update moves toward hiring a consultant
items.summary: The Historical and Landmarks Commission's November 5 agenda listed the selection of one commissioner to serve on the review board that will choose a consultant for the Historic Preservation Ordinance update. The update would revise the city's rules for protecting historic properties.

items.headline: Committee agenda: Ramona Street entertainment zone proposal
items.summary: The November 4 Economic Development Committee agenda listed a recommendation to the City Council to amend the Entertainment Zone Ordinance and establish an Entertainment Zone on Ramona Street. The item was marked as not a project under CEQA.

items.headline: Utilities commission agenda: reserve policy changes and FY 2028 rate projections
items.summary: The November 4 Utilities Advisory Commission agenda listed a staff recommendation to send the City Council updates to utility reserve practices. These cover a wastewater collection capital reserve and rate stabilization reserves for the electric, gas, water and wastewater collection utilities. The agenda also listed an update on the preliminary FY 2028 utilities financial forecast and rate projections.

items.headline: November 4 heritage agenda listed SB 9 lot-split changes
items.summary: The November 4 Heritage Preservation Commission agenda listed a presentation on recent changes to SB 9, including SB 450 and AB 1061, which altered rules for two-unit developments and urban lot splits in single-family zones. The same agenda listed a draft update to the city's Historical Context Statement to include contributions by Asian Americans and other minority groups.

items.headline: Technology Park plan has one pedestrian fix; traffic queues and a freeway bridge left open
items.summary: Staff said the project adds about 1,368 net daily car trips, with the only required mitigation being a mid-block crosswalk and upgraded crossing on Campbell Technology Park to McGlincy Lane. Queues at Curtner/White Oaks/Camden would rise from 30 to 32 vehicles, and a separate city restriping plan there is not a condition of approval. The developer agreed to record easements for a possible future pedestrian/bike bridge over Highway 17, but a feasibility-study grant application was unsuccessful, and the Planning Commission asked for 3-hour parking near Edith Morley Park.
